settings.tooltipAlpha: Customer importance blend weight. Applies to all journeys in this tenant. Alpha is the weight given to Importance to Customer versus Importance to Business when calculating a touchpoint's weight within its stage. A higher alpha means customer importance counts more; a lower alpha means business importance counts more. Beta is automatically set to (1 − alpha), so the two always sum to 1.0. Range 0.0–1.0, default 0.5 (balanced). Set higher (e.g., 0.7) if your programme prioritises the customer's perspective; set lower if commercial/compliance priorities should dominate scoring.
settings.tooltipMot: Score amplification applied to touchpoints flagged as a Moment of Truth (MoT) — the make-or-break interactions that disproportionately shape overall perception. A MoT touchpoint's weight in stage scoring is multiplied by this value; non-MoT touchpoints are unaffected (multiplier of 1.0). Range 1.0–2.0, default 1.5. Use 1.0 to disable MoT amplification entirely; raise toward 2.0 to make Moments of Truth dominate stage scores more strongly. The 2.0 cap prevents a single touchpoint from overwhelming the score.
settings.tooltipNFloor: The hard minimum number of responses a touchpoint must collect before its score is trusted. Below this floor, the touchpoint is marked "insufficient", excluded from scoring entirely, and shown as "—" rather than a number. This protects you from drawing conclusions from too few responses. Set higher if your tenant has high response volumes and you want stricter reliability; set lower for low-traffic programmes. It also acts as the flat threshold during a journey's first few weeks before enough history exists for adaptive thresholds.
settings.tooltipFlagPct: Sets how aggressively low-sample touchpoints are flagged as "low confidence". The system finds the response count at this percentile across all touchpoints in a journey; any touchpoint below it gets a low-sample badge. Default 25 (the bottom quarter by response volume is flagged). Valid range 1–49. Raise it (e.g., 30 or 32) to apply a stricter standard and flag more touchpoints as low-sample; lower it to flag fewer. This affects display/flagging only — it does not exclude touchpoints from scoring (that's the Responses Count Floor's job).
settings.tooltipRollingDays: The time window over which response counts are measured to compute the adaptive confidence thresholds (the median and the flag percentile). It is also the cold-start period: during a new journey's first window, the system falls back to the Responses Count Floor as a flat threshold until enough history accrues. Default 30 days, minimum 7. A 30-day window aligns with the typical expectation that meaningful journey data appears about a month after launch. Use a longer window for slower-moving programmes; a shorter one reacts faster but is noisier.
